title: Tokenized Reward Systems for Federated Learning: The Privacy vs. Fairness Tradeoff
read: Supplied PDF in full; equations and result tables visually checked.
problem: Quality disclosure and threshold proofs create different reward incentives.
method: Compares public cosine quality with a threshold-gated reward contract and analyzes noise self-inclusion.
data: MNIST with heterogeneous clients, free-riders and local contract execution.
finding: Reports increasing noise rewards during convergence and higher adversary capture under its threshold allocation.
missing: Does not test its proposed excluding-reference, history and slashing mitigations against poisoning or honest DP noise; uses a verifier stub.
use: Reproduction target and motivating failure mechanism. Published figures are comparison data, not our results.

title: Decentral and Incentivized Federated Learning Frameworks: A Systematic Literature Review
read: Abstract, systematic-review procedure, evaluation criteria and future-research sections; journal metadata cross-checked with DBLP.
problem: Decentralized incentive frameworks lack comparable implementation and evaluation evidence.
method: Systematic search and screening with a taxonomy of blockchain, incentive and learning choices.
data: Published federated-learning frameworks, rather than a newly trained benchmark.
finding: Identifies incomplete performance evaluation and scalability analysis as recurring gaps.
missing: Does not experimentally resolve the later cosine self-inclusion problem.
use: Motivates common-update comparisons and reporting computation and settlement costs together.

title: Free-rider Attacks on Model Aggregation in Federated Learning
venue: AISTATS, Proceedings of Machine Learning Research
read: Publisher abstract and BibTeX; PDF attack model, experimental methods, results and discussion.
problem: Clients can acquire the global model without supplying useful local training.
method: Analyzes unchanged-model and stochastically disguised updates under model averaging, including decaying perturbations.
data: MNIST, CIFAR-10 and Shakespeare under FedAvg and FedProx.
finding: Free-riders can obtain comparable final models while slowing convergence, especially at high participation fractions.
missing: Does not measure token capture or implement stake penalties and vesting.
use: Separates model-access free-riding from token extraction; motivates adaptive-noise attacks as a limitation of fixed-noise experiments.

title: Gradient-Driven Rewards to Guarantee Fairness in Collaborative Machine Learning
authors: Xu, Lyu, Ma, Miao, Foo, Low
read: Publisher abstract; PDF valuation, approximation, reputation, gradient-reward equations and experimental results.
problem: Contribution rewards should distinguish update quality without an auxiliary validation dataset.
method: Defines cosine coalition value, approximates its Shapley allocation, smooths contributions and rewards clients with differently sparsified global gradients.
data: MNIST, CIFAR-10, movie reviews and Stanford sentiment data.
finding: Reports competitive predictive performance and contribution-sensitive gradient rewards.
missing: Original rewards are gradients, not transferable tokens; an on-chain shadow allocation is an adaptation and cannot inherit its training guarantee automatically.
use: Extension rule and a test of self-inclusion under normalized, reputation-weighted references.

title: A Reputation Mechanism Is All You Need: Collaborative Fairness and Adversarial Robustness in Federated Learning
read: Abstract, algorithm, reputation equations, data and attack settings, result tables and limitations.
problem: Equal global-model access gives weak incentives and permits malicious contributions.
method: Uses normalized reputation-weighted aggregation, cosine-based moving reputation, permanent removal and gradient-download quotas.
data: Image and sentiment benchmarks, with free-riders and several poisoning transformations.
finding: Reports strong accuracy and robustness in its tested settings; identifies difficulty separating similar honest and malicious gradients.
missing: Does not evaluate exact token settlement or the false penalties caused by honest client-level DP noise.
use: Extension comparison; its removal and training feedback must be distinguished from our fixed-trajectory shadow adaptation.
